title: UDX: correct sequence analysis and reassembly
description:
Follow-up to !25989, which added the dissector. Six corrections to the sequence analysis: the first three reported by James Thomas of the libudx team, the rest found by comparing the dissector's verdicts against an instrumented build of libudx over its own test suite.Six problems in the stateful analysis. The first three were found in review by James Thomas; the rest came from comparing the dissector's verdicts against an instrumented build of libudx, packet by packet, over its own test suite.

A selective acknowledgement acknowledges a packet just as a cumulative one does, but only the cumulative path retired a segment. A packet named in a SACK block now records the frame that first acknowledged it, whether that was a selective or a cumulative acknowledgement, and leaves the flight at that point rather than staying counted as outstanding until the cumulative acknowledgement caught up. Both paths retire through one place, so a packet that is selectively acknowledged and later covered by a cumulative acknowledgement is not counted twice. The cumulative walk now steps over segments already retired instead of stopping at the first one, which it has to do once selective acknowledgements can retire packets out of order.

A retransmission that arrived after a full timeout was reported as a fast retransmission whenever the peer had selectively acknowledged anything above it. The elapsed time is the stronger signal, so the timeout is now tested first and the selective acknowledgement state only classifies retransmissions that arrive sooner than that.

A tail loss probe does not have to repeat the tail: libudx sends the next new packet as the probe when it has one. Such a packet is now recognised by what it looks like from outside - a fresh sequence number extending the flow after a probe-sized pause, with earlier data still unacknowledged.

Payload held back waiting for a gap ahead of it was never released once a second copy of a held packet reached the delivery point first, which happens whenever a retransmission arrives while an earlier gap is still open. The spent copy stayed at the head of the pending list and stopped everything behind it, so following a stream that had lost anything returned a fraction of the transfer and then stopped. Superseded copies are now discarded rather than left to block the queue. On a 256 KB transfer with induced loss this takes the reassembled payload from 32 KB to the whole of it.

The first packet seen on a flow is not always the one with the lowest sequence number: if it was lost and resent it arrives after its successors. The lowest sequence seen is now tracked separately from the first, and bounds the cumulative walk, so a packet below the first one seen is still retired instead of being counted as in flight for the rest of the capture.

A round trip time sample was credited to the flow that carried the acknowledgement rather than the flow whose packet it timed, while the retransmission timeout derived from it is judged on the sending flow. On a transfer carrying data in both directions the two samples were merely exchanged, but on a one-way transfer the sending flow never obtained a round trip time at all and every timeout test fell back on its floor.

Adds five captures and six tests covering the cases above.

         assert sorted(set(stdout.split('\n')[0].split('\t'))) == ['', '0']
         assert grep_output(stdout, r'^0\t1$')
 
+    def test_udx_rto_beats_sack(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
+        '''A full timeout decides a retransmission, even with later SACKs.
+
+        Sequence 0 is lost while 1 and 2 arrive and are selectively
+        acknowledged, so the highest selectively acknowledged sequence sits
+        above the resent one. The resend still comes a second and a half
+        later, which makes it a timer retransmission rather than a fast one.
+        '''
+        stdout = subprocess.check_output((cmd_tshark, *UDX_HEUR, '-2',
+                '-r', capture_file('udx_rto.pcap.gz'),
+                '-V',
+            ), encoding='utf-8', env=test_env)
+        assert grep_output(stdout, 'Retransmission timeout')
+        assert not grep_output(stdout, 'Fast retransmission')
+
+    def test_udx_sack_acknowledges(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
+        '''A selective acknowledgement acknowledges the packet it names.'''
+        stdout = subprocess.check_output((cmd_tshark, *UDX_HEUR, '-2',
+                '-r', capture_file('udx_rto.pcap.gz'),
+                '-Tfields', '-eframe.number', '-eudx.analysis.acked_in',
+            ), encoding='utf-8', env=test_env)
+        # Sequences 1 and 2 are acknowledged by the first SACK, in frame 4,
+        # not by the cumulative acknowledgement that arrives in frame 7.
+        assert grep_output(stdout, r'^2\t4$')
+        assert grep_output(stdout, r'^3\t4$')
+
+    def test_udx_tail_loss_probe_with_new_data(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
+        '''A probe that carries new data is still a probe.'''
+        stdout = subprocess.check_output((cmd_tshark, *UDX_HEUR, '-2',
+                '-r', capture_file('udx_tlpnew.pcap.gz'),
+                '-V',
+            ), encoding='utf-8', env=test_env)
+        assert grep_output(stdout, 'Tail loss probe')
+
     def test_udx_follow_stream(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
         '''Following a stream yields the payload in both directions.'''
         stdout = subprocess.check_output((cmd_tshark, *UDX_HEUR,
@@ -1501,6 +1535,49 @@ class TestDissectUdx:
 
         assert payload('udx_clean.pcap.gz')[-20:] == payload('udx_loss.pcap.gz')[-20:]
 
+    def test_udx_follow_superseded_fragment(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
+        '''A held packet that is delivered by another copy stops holding up
+        the ones behind it.
+
+        Sequence 2 is held while the gap at 1 is open and arrives a second
+        time before that gap closes. Filling the gap delivers one copy; the
+        other has to be discarded rather than left at the head of the pending
+        list, where it would block every packet after it.
+        '''
+        stdout = subprocess.check_output((cmd_tshark, *UDX_HEUR,
+                '-r', capture_file('udx_followstall.pcap.gz'),
+                '-q', '-z', 'follow,udx,ascii,0',
+            ), encoding='utf-8', env=test_env)
+        # All six packets, in sequence order, including the one sent last.
+        payload = [l for l in stdout.splitlines() if l and set(l) <= set('abcdef')]
+        assert ''.join(payload) == ''.join(c * 16 for c in 'abcdef')
+
+    def test_udx_acknowledges_below_first_seen(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
+        '''The first packet on the wire need not hold the lowest sequence.
+
+        Sequence 0 was lost and resent, so it appears after 1 and 2. The
+        cumulative acknowledgement covers all three and has to retire it.
+        '''
+        stdout = subprocess.check_output((cmd_tshark, *UDX_HEUR, '-2',
+                '-r', capture_file('udx_lateseq.pcap.gz'),
+                '-Tfields', '-eframe.number', '-eudx.analysis.acked_in',
+            ), encoding='utf-8', env=test_env)
+        assert grep_output(stdout, r'^3\t4$')
+
+    def test_udx_rtt_measured_on_sending_flow(self, cmd_tshark, capture_file, test_env):
+        '''The round trip time belongs to the flow whose packet was timed.
+
+        Only one side sends data here, so if the sample were credited to the
+        flow carrying the acknowledgements the sending flow would never have
+        one, and this six millisecond pause would fall under the floor that
+        applies when no round trip time is known.
+        '''
+        stdout = subprocess.check_output((cmd_tshark, *UDX_HEUR, '-2',
+                '-r', capture_file('udx_rtttlp.pcap.gz'),
+                '-V',
+            ), encoding='utf-8', env=test_env)
+        assert grep_output(stdout, 'Tail loss probe')
